summary: Misaligned queue depth thresholds cause autoscaler slow-to-react and transient GPU shortages for dedicated customer
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightLedger reported recurring mid-morning throughput degradation in their dedicated pool that manifests as sudden p50/p95 increases and intermittent 504s for short-lived embedding calls while a subset of long-lived search streams remain healthy. Impact first seen 2026-03-10 08:45 PDT.

Impact:
- Customer experiencing ~2-3x p95 latency spikes for embedding endpoint and occasional 504s for short requests across several nodes in their reserved pool.
- Business impact: data pipeline backpressure causing delayed analytics ingestion for BrightLedger’s ETL window.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer-managed capacity) in us-west-2
- Pool configured with autoscaler thresholds: queue_depth_avg > 12 triggers scale-up, queue_depth_p95 > 8 is logged but not used to trigger.
- Workloads: mix of long-lived streaming search sessions (low CPU, sustained GPU KV cache) and high-frequency, short-lived embedding requests (~5-20 tokens, high QPS).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Run a steady stream of ~30 long-lived search streams pinned to model redwood/open-vicuna-13b.
2) Ramp embedding calls to redwood/embedding-lite-v1 at 300 rps with ~10 token responses.
3) Observe: short embedding calls see rising tail latency and intermittent 504s after ~7–10 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- Autoscaler delayed scale-up by ~4 minutes after tail latency increased.
- GPUs on 3 hosts reported elevated utilization but queue_depth_avg remained under threshold because the long-lived streams inflate active slot occupancy while short requests create transient bursts that spike p95.
- Telemetry shows periodic NVLINK and PCIe stalls on the affected hosts coincident with the bursts.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should react within the configured SLO window to the short-lived request burst or alternative route to fallback model variants to prevent 504s.

Logs / metrics / links:
- Customer-provided traces: s3://brightledger-support/traces/2026-03-10-08-45.zip
- Console charts (token-level): https://console.redwood.ai/customers/brightledger/pool/metrics?window=15m
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C01SUPPORT/p1623
- Related incident: INC-2026-45 (low-level NVLINK error stream from 2026-03-09)

Workaround in place:
- Support temporarily increased autoscaler sensitivity (queue_depth_avg threshold lowered) and enabled short-request routing to burst-hot fallback model variant. This reduced 504s but did not fully prevent p95 spikes.
comments: Support (Marisol): 2026-03-10 09:02 PDT - Customer reports first occurrence during their ETL window. Asked for traces and recent console links.
Customer (BrightLedger Ops): 2026-03-10 09:12 PDT - Uploaded traces and confirmed they saw dozens of 504s concentrated on three hosts. Not all workloads affected (search streams fine).
SRE (Ethan): 2026-03-10 09:30 PDT - Identified autoscaler did not use p95 queue metric to trigger scale. Will run hypothesis tests against metric selection and host telemetry.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:35 PDT - Pulled autoscaler decision logs for pool: autoscaler signed decisions show queue_depth_avg=9.2 at 09:20 while queue_depth_p95=14.8. The code path only evaluated queue_depth_avg for scale-up events for dedicated pools (confirmed via autoscaler logs).

2026-03-10 10:00 PDT - Correlated serving-runtime logs: short-lived requests show high enqueue/dequeue churn leading to head-of-queue stalls when long-lived sessions hold prefetched KV state.\nTelemetry indicates NVLINK error counters increased ~2x on hosts A,B,C during bursts (see internal metric stream).

2026-03-10 10:25 PDT - Replayed customer load in staging with similar mix; reproduced p95 spikes when autoscaler uses average thresholds. When we switched the test autoscaler to consider queue_depth_p95 > 8 as a trigger, scale-up happened within 45s and tail latency drop recovered.

Hypothesis: Autoscaler using only average queue depth causes slow reaction for mixed workloads with long-lived session occupancy. Short bursts inflate p95 and cause transient GPU backpressure (plus NVLINK stalls), but average remains low because long streams keep GPU slots busy.

Action items (ongoing): test autoscaler logic change in canary, evaluate possible on-host NVLINK error rate mitigation, and add customer-specific routing option for short embeddings to separate pools or fallback variants.
resolution:
Workaround applied: lowered queue_depth_avg threshold for BrightLedger dedicated pool and enabled routing rule to send embedding calls to a burst-dedicated fallback variant. Canary autoscaler change (evaluate p95 as additional trigger) merged and deployed to canary (see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1823).

Permanent next steps:
- Roll out autoscaler enhancement to honor configurable percentile triggers (p95) for scale-up decisions in dedicated pools (planned rollout 2026-03-18, ops runbook updated).
- Investigate NVLINK error trend on affected host SKU (hardware telemetry forwarded to infra engineering; tracking INT-2026-88).
- Add new console setting to allow customers to opt into "short-request isolation" routing for mixed workload pools.

Customer status: BrightLedger accepted workaround; ETL window completed on 2026-03-11 with reduced impact. Follow-ups scheduled with Solutions Engineering to discuss longer-term routing configuration.
